title: Renewal & expansion check-in - Riverbend Logistics

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Emma Clarke (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Riverbend CTO), Miguel Santos (Head of Infrastructure), Sarah Lee (Procurement)
Shared links: pricing deck (link), SOC2 summary (link), benchmark prompt set (uploaded to shared drive)

Summary (auto): Quick check on renewal options and expansion needs. Riverbend wants extra capacity for peak season, add EU region for data residency, and wants clearer SLAs for p99. Agreed to run benchmarks and provide updated pricing.

Transcript:
[00:00] Emma Clarke: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, happy Valentines day, uh, we'll try and keep this to 45 minutes. I'm Emma from Redwood, with Raj on the line, and from Riverbend we have Laura, Miguel and Sarah.
[00:12] Laura Kim: Hey, thanks Emma. Quick status: contract up in 6 weeks, so we're looking at renewal plus a possible capacity bump and EU region.
[00:20] Raj Patel: Great, thanks. Do you have a sense of the capacity bump — like sustained or burst?
[00:27] Miguel Santos: It's both, honestly. Our peak load for last quarter spiked about 2.8x for short windows, and sustained growth about 30% year over year. We're looking at reserved capacity for baseline and burst for unexpected surges.
[00:38] Emma Clarke: Makes sense. We typically recommend Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput. We can size a reserved pool and leave a burst policy — the pricing deck I shared shows tiers.
[00:49] Sarah Lee: From procurement's side we want term options: 1-year vs 3-year, and better per-unit pricing for a commit. Also need formal SLAs for p50/p95/p99.
[00:59] Raj Patel: For p99 we'd aim for the Dedicated pool with autoscale headroom; also caching + KV cash — uh K-V cache — helps for repeat prefixes. Not perfect transcription there, but the main point is prefix/KV cache reduces cost and latency.
[01:18] Laura Kim: On the EU region: due to data residency regs we need logs and result retention to remain in EU for EU users. How do you support that on Private vs Dedicated?
[01:27] Emma Clarke: For Redwood Dedicated we can provision capacity in eu-west-1 and restrict data plane so that inference and logs stay in-region. For Private we provide a customer-managed control plane option. We'll include the exact audit log retention details in the SOC2 doc.
[01:40] Miguel Santos: Is KMS integration available? We need to use our HSM for key management.
[01:44] Raj Patel: Yes, KMS/HSM integration is supported — we have customer-managed key policies and the option to rotate keys. I will attach the HSM integration guide.
[01:52] Sarah Lee: Any gotchas on migrating existing routes? Our infra is on GCP — we use VPC peering and some on-prem connectors.
[01:59] Emma Clarke: We've done a number of GCP customers; VPC peering and private networking options are supported. We can route by region/tier. There might be some small network NACL tweaks but nothing major.
[02:12] Laura Kim: What about fallbacks — if Dedicated runs out of capacity mid-peak, can you fall back to hosted models automatically?
[02:19] Raj Patel: Yes, smart routing can fall back to a compatible model variant in the hosted pool to preserve availability. There is a policy you can set for cost-first or latency-first.
[02:30] Miguel Santos: We care about deterministic latency for customer-facing features — our p99 SLA internal is 200ms. Can you meet that?
[02:37] Raj Patel: For shorter sequences and optimized kernels we can get under 200ms p99 on Dedicated, depending on model family and quantization. We'll validate on the benchmark with your prompt set, because sequence length matters a lot.
[02:50] Laura Kim: We also have some sensitive PII in prompts — how does Redwood handle data retention and deletion?
[02:56] Emma Clarke: We support in-transit and at-rest encryption, audit logs, and data retention policies. For Dedicated/Private we can set zero-retention for logs or ensure logs remain in-customer storage. We'll include explicit language for deletion in the SOW/contract.
[03:12] Sarah Lee: Procurement will need SOC2 Type II report and a data processing agreement.
[03:17] Emma Clarke: Yes, I've uploaded the SOC2 summary; legal can get the DPA template.
[03:22] Laura Kim: Pricing: your last renewal had per-token pricing plus an overage. We're hoping to move more to committed capacity pricing.
[03:29] Emma Clarke: Right. The three options we typically present: 1) continue hosted with higher overage rates, 2) Dedicated reserved with monthly commit and lower unit economics, or 3) Dedicated with multi-year commit for best pricing. There's also burst credits. I'll put exact numbers in the revised deck.
[03:47] Miguel Santos: On metrics we want per-route dashboards and token-level cost — can we see that in the console?
[03:53] Raj Patel: Yes, Redwood Console gives per-route breakdowns, token costs, traces, and error analysis. We can add custom tags for your routes.
[04:02] Laura Kim: For the benchmark, what do you need from us?
[04:06] Raj Patel: We'll need the sample prompt set, expected percentiles for sequence length, target concurrency, and a preferred region. We already have the prompt set in the shared drive; Miguel, can you confirm concurrency profile?
[04:16] Miguel Santos: I'll pull our k6 traces and send a profile — expect to have that today.
[04:20] Emma Clarke: Great. We'll run a 24-hour throughput run with your prompts to capture steady-state and spike behavior. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and token/unit cost.
[04:29] Sarah Lee: On contracts, we need a clear termination clause and exit data export.
[04:33] Emma Clarke: Standard SOW includes exit export and a 60-day notice for non-renewal. We can negotiate termination penalties for multi-year commits.
[04:40] Laura Kim: Competitors — we did a quick spike with Run:AI internally and also evaluated Vertex. Your pricing last year was competitive vs OpenAI for in-house models. We'd like to see an apples-to-apples compute + license comparison.
[04:54] Raj Patel: We can include a cost model workbook showing reserved vs on-demand and token-level math. We'll highlight where caching and quantization change the economics.
[05:03] Emma Clarke: Ok let's recap next steps — action items.
[05:07] Miguel Santos: Quick question, is there an option to bring the runtime on-prem as a temporary hot-fix?
[05:11] Raj Patel: We have an on-prem package for regulated workloads, but it's heavier weight. For your needs (data residency + EU region) Dedicated in-region should be simpler. If you need fully air-gapped, we can discuss Private.
[05:25] Sarah Lee: Sounds good.
[05:27] Emma Clarke: Great recap: 1) Emma to send revised pricing + 3-year option by Feb 18. 2) Raj to run 24-hour benchmark and share results by Feb 25. 3) Miguel to send traffic profiles by EOD Feb 16. 4) Schedule a 30-minute follow-up week of Feb 22. Anything else?
[05:46] Laura Kim: That's it, thanks. We'll prioritize the profile exports.
[06:00] Emma Clarke: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments and a calendar invite.
[44:30] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap and minor mis-hearings ("K-V cash" for KV cache, "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated").
